description: Every place untrusted bytes enter the Rust agent, who can put them there, the code that first reads them, and the fuzz targets (crates/host-agent/src/fuzzing.rs, fuzz/) and property tests (crates/host-agent/src/properties.rs) that cover it. fuzzing::tests::inventory checks this file against the code: every entry has coverage, every named target and property exists, and every target is listed.

entries.code: http1::read_request (request line, URI, MIME headers, Host checks)

entries.source: the same peer
entries.code: http1::Body (Content-Length, chunked, Expect: 100-continue, post-handler discard; read_all's bound, D29 and D41)

entries.source: an MCP client, authenticated or not
entries.code: transport::route -> mcp; gojson::parse, first_value, syntax_error; mcpsdk::serve

findings.summary: Uri::new accepted a resource id with Unicode whitespace other than space, tab, CR or LF (U+000B, U+000C, U+0085, U+2003, ...); Uri::parse of the printed URI trimmed it, so the identity changed. The spec says IDs are not rewritten.
transport::basic_auth sliced the Authorization header at byte 6; a header with a multi-byte character there panicked the connection's task on /oauth/token (no reply; the agent kept serving).
findings.state: fixed: the prefix is compared as bytes

findings.summary: /mcp read an authenticated request's whole body into memory before the 4 MiB limit.

gojson decoded a \u escape with u32::from_str_radix, which accepts a leading sign, so "\u+019" parsed while Go's scanner (and RFC 8259) reject it: a tools/call body Go refuses as invalid JSON was accepted. The same sign-accepting decode was fixed in transport's =XX decode, the llmops relay's %XX path decode and its chunk-size parse.
findings.foundBy: fuzz target json_document (parser/scanner oracle), pass 3, 23 s
findings.state: fixed: four hex digits are required before decoding (no D-number: the contract and Go already reject)

findings.summary: With the state directory full, an effectful call (ensure_host_file, run_host_command) still ran on the host; its audit row was written after the call and the failed write was ignored, so the change went unrecorded. D31 requires the call to be refused.
findings.state: fixed: effectful calls are refused with state_storage_full before they run while under 1 MiB is free (D31)

findings.summary: /health ran incus list on the single thread that serves every connection; an incus that never exits stalled every request, including tools/list, for its 45 s timeout per health check.
findings.state: fixed: /health runs on the blocking pool, as tools/call does

findings.summary: The state store keeps one capability-invocation row per call (about 3.5 KB each for the e2e6.budget mix) and never prunes them; under 28,144 calls in 15 minutes it grew 81.5 MB. The spec states durable audit but no retention, so this is growth by contract, not a leak.
findings.state: fixed by D42 (openspec/changes/audit-retention): 30 days and 50,000 rows by default, pruned in the background

findings.summary: The model-serving relay read an inference request's whole body before forwarding it, with no bound.

Every process the agent started inherited the agent's whole environment, MCP_AUTH_TOKEN, OPUTE_OAUTH_CLIENTS and provider credentials included: incus, kubectl, git, curl, ollama and the systemd-run client all received them. A caller's own run_host_command ran in a systemd unit and did not.
findings.foundBy: m15 review of the console spawn
findings.state: fixed by D40 (openspec/changes/child-process-environment): an allowlist at every spawn site

findings.summary: A provider executable's /mcp read a request's whole body before the SDK's 4 MiB limit, as /mcp did before D29.
findings.state: fixed by D41 (openspec/changes/bound-relay-request-body): the SDK's 4 MiB, 413 beyond
